body.html: Wangnamyen Garden Hotel sits at 299 Moo 10, Wang Nam Yen Subdistrict, Wang Nam Yen District — a hotel on the main road that runs through the centre of Wang Nam Yen · It's a place locals and road-trippers along this route know well, since it's right on the main road, easy to find, and the district's main hotel choice (TripAdvisor ranks it #1 of 1 hotels in Wang Nam Yen). That makes it a handy overnight stop on the way through.

What guests mention most is the spacious, clean rooms and good hot-water bathrooms · Many reviews say rooms are larger than expected for the price, with fresh, clean linen and towels · The hotel has two buildings — a Standard building and a slightly upgraded Superior building · Rooms come with air conditioning, a water heater, TV and free Wi-Fi, enough for an overnight stay · Several road-tripping foreign guests call it good value for a single night.
"Clean, nicely spacious room, water flowing, bright lights, cool air-con — a hotel you can book with confidence for a stop in Wang Nam Yen."

Another frequent compliment is the friendly, helpful staff and the easy-to-find main-road location · There's an on-site restaurant/bar for simple meals and breakfast · And for self-drivers there's free private parking, so there's no worry about where to leave the car · Some reviews praise breakfast as well laid out with a decent variety, though a few note items can be slow to refill.

The honest caveats — the building and bathrooms are starting to show their age · Some reviews note dated-looking bathrooms and a shower head fitted a little low · There are occasional reports of ants in some rooms, so it's worth keeping snacks and food sealed away · Opinions on the hotel restaurant's food are mixed — some like it, others find it ordinary · And staff speak limited English, so foreign travellers may want a translation app on hand.

In short, Wangnamyen Garden Hotel suits anyone wanting a spacious, clean, affordable room on the Wang Nam Yen main road, for an overnight stop on the way through or a trip into the district · An overall score of about 7.3 from real reviews reflects exactly that — roomy and good value with friendly staff, but with an ageing building and a few small details to factor in · Set your expectations and lean on the value, and most guests have a comfortable night.

tips.title: Ask for the Superior building for newer rooms
tips.body: The hotel has two buildings — if you want a room in better condition and a bit larger, ask for the Superior building when booking or at check-in. It costs a little more but is more comfortable.

tips.title: Keep food sealed away
tips.body: Some reviews report ants in certain rooms. Keep snacks and food in sealed bags and take rubbish outside the room before bed — it helps a lot.

tips.title: Have a translation app ready
tips.body: Staff speak limited English. If you're a foreign traveller, have a translation app ready to smooth check-in and ordering food.

tips.title: Use it as a stop before town or the border
tips.body: Wang Nam Yen is on a through-route, so it works as an overnight stop before driving on to Sa Kaeo town or Aranyaprathet and the Rong Kluea Market.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Wangnamyen Garden Hotel, Sa Kaeo

faq.q: Where is Wangnamyen Garden Hotel in Sa Kaeo?
faq.a: It's at 299 Moo 10, Wang Nam Yen Subdistrict, Wang Nam Yen District, Sa Kaeo, on the main road through the district and easy to find · It's the district's main hotel choice, with an onward drive of about 40 minutes to Sa Kaeo town and about 1.5 hours to Aranyaprathet and the Rong Kluea Market.

faq.q: What's the starting price and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rooms start from about THB 560/night for a Standard room · There's a Standard building and an upgraded Superior building at around THB 700–750 · Prices vary by season, so compare across platforms before booking.

faq.q: What are the rooms like — are they spacious?
faq.a: The standout is spacious, clean rooms with good hot-water bathrooms, larger than expected at this price, with air-con, TV and free Wi-Fi · The building shows its age in places, so ask for the Superior building if you want a room in better condition.

faq.q: Is there parking and a pool?
faq.a: There is free private parking, ideal for self-drivers · There is no swimming pool, but there's an on-site restaurant and bar, plus a breakfast service.

Opinions on breakfast are mixed — some reviews praise it as well laid out with a decent variety, others note items are slow to refill or fairly plain · Overall it's a basic breakfast for an overnight stay.

faq.q: Who is this hotel best for?
faq.a: It suits anyone wanting a spacious, clean, affordable room on the Wang Nam Yen main road, for an overnight stop on the way through or a trip into the district · Less suited to those wanting a new hotel or a resort with a swimming pool.
